_comment: qeli-ss-plugin standalone SERVER config (JSON).
Run:  qeli-ss-plugin --config standalone-server.json
No shadowsocks involved: the plugin listens on "listen", authenticates
tunnels, and forwards every demuxed stream to "remote" — ANY TCP service
(an HTTP server, sshd, a database, or ss-server if you still want it).
Key reference:
role      "client" or "server" (default client)
listen    THIS process's listener — the public entry point (required).
IPv4: "0.0.0.0:8443" (IPv4-only); IPv6 (bracketed):
"[::]:8443" (dual-stack on Linux by default; on some systems
binds IPv6-only — add a second listen via IPv4 if needed)
remote    where demuxed streams are forwarded ("forward" is an alias)
password  auth secret — REQUIRED; ONE password serves any number of
clients from any hosts (must match the clients)
key       the server identity PRIVATE key from `qeli-ss-plugin --genkey`
(keep it secret; clients pin the matching public key via
"serverkey")
ping      keepalive interval, seconds (0 = off); dead-peer detection is
bounded by ping + 2s
timeout   connect/handshake timeout, seconds
Note: sni/serverkey are CLIENT-side options (the SNI lives in the
ClientHello the client sends); the server side does not need them.
Unknown keys are a config error (a typo must not be silently ignored).
